transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-04-02
Start: 20:30 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Location: Zoom
Recording: auto

Summary (auto):
Short demo of Redwood streaming behavior under high TPS and long-context workloads, focused on graceful degradation and fallback strategies; covered KV cache eviction, streaming backpressure, partial-token delivery to mobile clients, and suggested Optimize/Console settings. Lots of questions on VPC/private deployment and encryption/KMS.

Topics:
- Streaming backpressure and partial tokens
- KV cache TTL and eviction impact on long sessions
- Graceful fallback to quantized/smaller model variants
- Per-route SLOs and traceability in Console
- Cost vs latency trade-offs (batching, caching, routing)
- Security: audit logs, KMS, SSO

Attendees:
Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nambiar (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (LuminaPay CTO), Elaine Wu (Lead ML Eng), Tom Hargreaves (Platform Eng), Marta Novak (Security)

00:00 Jordan: hey everyone thanks for joining from Redwood, i'm Jordan, i'm the account lead. priya here will run through the demo and the weird edge cases you hit with long contexts and mobile streaming.
00:20 Priya: hi all, quick agenda — show a live run that simulates 3k TPS with a mix of short and very long contexts, then toggle kv cache eviction to see behavior, show fallback to a quantized 8-bit model, then walk the console alerts and cost breakdown.
00:40 Samir: sounds good. our main worry is partial responses on mobile — if the stream gets cut we don't want duplicate charges or half-rendered UI. also we run VPC private for PII endpoints.
01:05 Priya: yep, that's exactly what we'll simulate, also demonstrate the "resume token" pattern with session IDs; note that's an app-level pattern not built into the streaming HTTP chunking itself.
01:35 Elaine: quick question — does Redwood support resuming a truncated streaming chunk mid-token, or do we always re-request from last final token?
01:50 Priya: currently the runtime doesn't splice a token mid-byte, so you either get what was flushed; for resumed flows we recommend the prefix cache + token-index pattern — we can demo that in the SDK later. sometimes transcripts show re-flow as 're-stream' which is inconsistent, i know.
02:20 Tom: also, about KV cache — when eviction happens we saw huge tail-latency spikes in our internal tests. curious what your mitigation knobs are.
02:40 Priya: good call. so the runtime exposes cache TTL and a hot-key pinning option per-route, and the console shows eviction rate. when cache is evicted you see cold-start overhead for KV load which manifests as a 150-400ms extra per-request in our runs depending on model size.
03:10 Jordan: and that's where graceful fallback matters — you can route to a smaller model variant or an 8-bit quantized variant automatically when latency spikes or when queue depth passes threshold. that reduces token quality slightly but keeps latency within SLO.
03:45 Marta: security stuff — for private deployments we need KMS integration + HSM support and audit logs retained for 1 year. does Redwood offer that?
04:00 Jordan: yes, private customers get KMS/HSM integrations, we emit audit events to your SIEM and Console retains an audit trail; retention windows are configurable. we'll send the security pack after the call.
04:28 Samir: competitor question — does this differ from OpenAI's hosted endpoints? we care about predictable tail latency under surge.
04:40 Priya: yes — OpenAI is more single-tenant hosted; our differentiator is routing + autoscaling + per-route SLOs + dedicated capacity for committed customers; also console-level tracing ties requests to tokens and KV hit metrics which helps debug tail spikes.
05:15 Priya: demo start — i've kicked off a synthetic driver: 3k TPS, 20% long-contexts (8k tokens), rest short. streaming to a simulated mobile aggregator that drops connections randomly to simulate backpressure.
05:40 (sound of terminal, brief pause)
06:02 Priya: ok, you can see in the Console the queue depth rising at 3k TPS for the long-context route, and the per-route latency chart starts to drift. note the 'kv eviction rate' metric on the right.
06:28 Elaine: i see a spike to 1.2s for p95 on that route, and some streams show 'partial chunk' events. what causes the partial chunking?
06:42 Priya: partial chunks happen when the runtime flushes partial tokens due to chunk-timeouts — it's an optimization to reduce perceived latency but under backpressure you may get many small chunks which on mobile cause more render work. we expose a chunking config in Optimize to tune chunk size, flush interval, and token threshold.
07:10 Tom: and when a mobile client reconnects, do we dedupe charges? curious about billing semantics.
07:25 Jordan: billing is per-token served. for resumed flows you should re-request from the last confirmed token index; duplicates mean duplicate tokens billed — so the recommended pattern is to use a confirmation ACK from client before advancing billing-critical state, or use server-side prefix cache to avoid re-generation.
07:58 Samir: so there's an app-level contract we need. okay.
08:20 Priya: i'm toggling KV TTL from 10m to 1m for the long-context route — watch the eviction rate and the p95.
08:36 (CLI click)
08:50 Priya: eviction rate jumps, p95 goes up ~300ms; on the streaming side we start seeing chunk retransmits on 1% of sessions where the stream dropped.
09:15 Elaine: can the runtime buffer partial tokens server-side so reconnecting clients can pick up exactly where they left off?
09:28 Priya: we can keep a short-lived session prefix in memory but that requires memory commitment; for very large scale we recommend a small durable prefix cache (redis or local LRU) with a session ID. Console shows your prefix hit rate so you can tune capacity.
10:02 Tom: what's the fallback routing policy look like? priority order?
10:16 Priya: default is: 1) try the pinned dedicated pool, 2) if queue depth exceeds X or latency breaches SLO, route to a quantized variant in the same pool, 3) if still constrained, route to a smaller architecture in a lower-cost pool. all configurable per-route in the Console.
10:48 Samir: that routing change — how transparent is it to the app? do we get token-level annotations that a fallback occurred?
11:02 Priya: yes we add a header in the response and an event in the trace that notes fallback_reason and fallback_variant; you can set alerts for fallback percent.
11:30 Marta: compliance — we need to ensure fallback logs don't leak PII.
11:40 Jordan: audit events can be redacted at ingestion and redwood supports field-level masking before logs are retained. we'll include the masking options in the security pack.
12:05 Priya: now i'll simulate a severe backpressure event — drop 20% of connections and increase arrival burst. watch the 'session tailback' metric.
12:28 (brief network chatter)
12:55 Priya: okay we see increased session tailback, console draws a waterfall of queued chunks, and our automatic shedding rule triggers which starts rejecting low-priority requests with 429 while keeping high-priority payment auth endpoints healthy.
13:20 Samir: good — can we set per-customer priority on requests? like some merchants are premium?
13:33 Priya: yes per-route priority and token-level priority via metadata headers. optimize suggests priority buckets based on cost sensitivity.
13:50 Tom: about per-route SLOs — how are they enforced? is it only alerting or true denial/fallback policies?
14:05 Priya: both — Console enforces soft SLOs with alerts and can auto-apply fallback policies; hard SLOs are configured as quota limits that will reject when exceeded.
14:28 Elaine: cli jargon in transcript said 'KV cash' earlier — lol that's the transcript autocorrect, meant 'KV cache'.
14:40 (laughter)
15:02 Priya: i'm going to force a fallback now to the quantized 8-bit variant. you should see a slight quality regression on the long completion but p99 latency improves notably.
15:28 (typing sounds)
15:45 Priya: ok fallback active. p99 dropped from 2.1s to 1.0s on long-context route. you can also see token-delta histograms in Console indicating a slight change in logits distribution.
16:10 Elaine: can we A/B test fallback to measure user-facing impact?
16:20 Priya: yes the rollout tool supports canary and A/B tests with automatic rollback if a quality metric (you define) regresses. we also tie to evaluation harnesses so you can run prompt sets and check rouge/bleu-ish metrics or custom LTV metrics.
17:03 Samir: what about on-premises private deployment? latency-wise would that change anything?
17:18 Jordan: private gives you control of network topology so egress to mobile gateways can be faster; but you lose Redwood-managed autoscaling unless you opt for the managed private plane. still, same runtime logic applies.
17:50 Marta: encryption keys — can we rotate keys without downtime?
18:02 Jordan: yes KMS rotation is supported; we have key-rotation APIs and HSM-backed keys for private customers. rotation can be seamless if you follow the recommended dual-key rollover. we'll include details.
18:30 Tom: can you walk through the console alert that triggered during the test and the trace for one example session?
18:44 Priya: sure — picking session id LP-4f3b — here's the trace: request-in, model-load, kv-hit false, load-kv-from-store, token flush events, fallback event. note the timestamps show a 380ms KV load and a 220ms model compile for that session which caused the tail.
19:20 Elaine: transcription shows 'model compile' but for us that might be kernel selection time — is that configurable?
19:35 Priya: it's kernel selection and warmup; you can pin kernels via runtime flags if you trade flexibility for predictability. optimize will recommend kernel warming for your most common sequence lengths.
20:00 Samir: on billing — if we route to fallback model, is cost automatically lower? how would that reflect in invoices?
20:12 Jordan: fallback to a smaller model reduces per-token compute units and is reflected in per-route cost breakdown; Console shows token-cost per model variant and you can set e.g., cost cap alerts. invoicing still token-based.
20:45 Tom: any built-in dedupe for retries where network glitches cause re-sends?
21:00 Priya: we provide idempotency keys at the API layer for request-level dedupe, but streaming partial-chunk dedupe is app-level. idempotency helps with duplicate full requests.
21:30 Samir: could Redwood expose a streaming checksum to help clients detect duplication?
21:45 Priya: it's been requested, we can log a chunk-hash but the client would need to verify, it's on the roadmap.
22:10 (discussion of sample SDK patterns)
22:45 Priya: switching to Optimize: here the recommendation engine suggests increasing cache capacity for the long-context route, lowering flush-interval from 120ms to 80ms for perceived latency, and enabling a fallback policy that triggers at 85th percentile breach.
23:10 Elaine: will those changes affect cost materially?
23:25 Priya: increasing cache raises memory footprint (higher infra cost) but reduces per-token compute; in our sample sheet the break-even is around 2m tokens/day on that route. We'll attach that sheet.
23:52 Jordan: i'm pulling the benchmark CSV — note the experimental column that shows 'mobile partial chunk penalty' which is our internal heuristic for UX cost.
24:20 Samir: a lot of this looks promising. next, security team wants a runbook for incident where fallback caused a wrong completion — need rollback and immediate mitigation steps.
24:40 Jordan: good ask — we have a rollback playbook and immediate mitigation: 1) toggle fallback off, 2) pin to committed pool, 3) increase sampling evals for affected prompts. we will share the runbook PDF.
25:05 Marta: please make sure PII fields are masked in traces before we share real traces.
25:18 Jordan: agreed — we'll provide sanitized examples.
25:40 Priya: i'm going to run one more test — long context, then force client reconnects at token 4k; you'll see how the prefix cache helps avoid re-gen.
26:02 (typing)
26:22 Priya: reconnects triggered, sessions with prefix hits resumed at ~40ms to next token vs prefix miss at ~500ms. that's pretty big.
26:50 Elaine: can we set TTL on prefix cache per-route?
27:05 Priya: yes TTL per route and also hot-key pinning for specific session ids.
27:30 Tom: what about model-version pinning during a deployment? we saw regressions when models auto-updated.
27:44 Priya: you can pin model versions per-route and roll them via canary; Console shows diffed eval metrics pre/post.
28:10 Samir: any known gotchas on retries when using canary?
28:25 Priya: watch for cookie-sticky routing — retries might not hit the same variant if not sticky; you can enable sticky routing for session-id.
28:50 Jordan: quick recap: we showed streaming backpressure effects, KV eviction impact, fallback policy and quantized variant efficiency, prefix-cache resume, SDK patterns for dedupe, and Console recommendations from Optimize.
29:20 Jordan: next steps — we'll send the SLO playbook, the benchmark CSV, sanitized traces, and security pack. Priya will run the extended perf sim; LuminaPay will share traces and routes.
29:40 Samir: thanks, one more micro question — what's the expected timeline to run a pilot? we're targeting early may.
29:55 Jordan: that aligns — 2–3 week pilot prep, 4 week pilot once traces are ingested.
30:12 (end of formal demo; remaining time Q&A and clarifications)
30:40 — remainder of meeting covers small clarifs and re-iteration of tasks, some cross-talk and brief pauses, we ended around 21:32 UTC.
